shortTitle: HomID: a stress test for dimension estimators
summary: Different estimators can give very different answers for the same data. HomID tests them on curved spaces whose true dimension is known.
authors: Aritra Das, Joseph T. Iosue, Victor V. Albert
paperTitle: HomID: Benchmarking Intrinsic Dimension Estimators on Homogeneous Manifolds with Anisotropic Embeddings
animationLabel: A light sphere S² fades. A north-pole arrow stays fixed under SO(2) rotations around its axis. An SO(3) rotation carries it to another point. The groups combine into SO(3) / SO(2) ≅ S².
animationNote: SO(2) is the subgroup of SO(3) that fixes the chosen north-pole vector. The quotient is a homogeneous space, not a quotient group.
stages: Begin with the sphere S².
The coherent state method proceeds as follows.
Choose a north-pole direction.
A SO(2) rotation around the z-axis leaves north pole invariant.
A SO(3) rotation move the arrow to arbitrary point on the sphere.
Identify rotations that differ only by an SO(2) turn.
SO(3) / SO(2) ≅ S².

shortTitle: Learning to grok from in-context examples
summary: We use modular arithmetic to study when a transformer can combine learned skills and solve tasks it did not see during training.
authors: Tianyu He, Darshil Doshi, Aritra Das, Andrey Gromov
paperTitle: Learning to grok: Emergence of in-context learning and skill composition in modular arithmetic tasks
animationLabel: Examples reveal a hidden modular rule, followed by an exact answer to a new input.
animationNote: Exact arithmetic illustrates the task; no trained transformer is running here.
stages: Examples in the prompt describe a task.
The same weights must handle a new task.
Use the examples to answer a new question.

shortTitle: Solving arbitrary modular polynomials through architecture design.
summary: An exact network can solve a task that ordinary training struggles with. We explore this gap by composing analytical arithmetic circuits.
authors: Darshil Doshi, Tianyu He, Aritra Das, Andrey Gromov
animationLabel: Two exact modular multiplication operations are combined to evaluate a polynomial.
animationNote: An arithmetic schematic; not the full neural architecture or a training result.
stages: Compute two modular products.
Combine the expert computations.
The polynomial result follows exactly.

summary: Simple local rules generate patterns with very different behavior. We use these tasks to study the relationship between model depth and data complexity.
authors: Tianyu He, Darshil Doshi, Aritra Das, Andrey Gromov
paperTitle: Exploring model depth and data complexity through the lens of cellular automata
venue: Scientific Methods for Understanding Deep Learning, NeurIPS 2024 workshop
animationLabel: Elementary cellular automata rules 90 and 30 generate rows of binary cells from a single seed.
animationNote: Actual cellular automaton evolution; not a neural network prediction.
stages: A local rule updates each binary cell.
Repeated updates create a whole pattern.
Change the rule to change the data.

shortTitle: Generalizing sub-circuits and how to find them.
summary: We deliberately corrupt arithmetic labels to separate rule learning from memorization, then examine the neurons that support each behavior.
authors: Darshil Doshi, Aritra Das, Tianyu He, Andrey Gromov
paperTitle: To grok or not to grok: Disentangling generalization and memorization on corrupted algorithmic datasets
animationLabel: An arithmetic table acquires wrong labels, followed by a schematic separation and pruning of memorizing units.
animationNote: Conceptual neuron groups; colors and counts are not experimental measurements.
stages: Begin with a known modular arithmetic rule.
Some training answers are deliberately wrong.
Separate rule learning from memorized exceptions.

shortTitle: Fractionalized holes in a one-dimensional gauge theory
summary: Near full filling, a hole can separate two shifted quantum backgrounds. We study the resulting motion, entanglement, and emergent integrability.
authors: Aritra Das, Umberto Borla, Sergej Moroz
paperTitle: Fractionalized holes in one-dimensional Z₂ gauge theory coupled to fermion matter: Deconfined dynamics and emergent integrability
animationLabel: A hole moves between two shifted electric-link backgrounds, moving the domain wall with it.
animationNote: Schematic domain-wall motion; not simulated quantum dynamics.
stages: Two backgrounds differ by one lattice translation.
A hole separates the two electric-link patterns.
Moving the hole moves the boundary.
